She finds a pair of folding chairs, an old washstand and a collection of glass bottles. Upholsterer Simion Hawtin-Smith and upcycler Sarah Parmenter set to work helping Jacqui transform her finds, but will all three projects produce profits?

programme.title: Escape to the Country
programme.desc: Having spent many happy family holidays in Cornwall, a couple from Hertfordshire now want to make England’s most south-westerly county their permanent home, and Steve Brown is just the man to help them realise their dream. The trio also meet a local ceramicist and take part in a pottery throwdown.

programme.title: The Bidding Room
programme.desc: Nigel Havers presides as members of the public with interesting items to sell come face to face with five dealers who bid against each other to try to bag themselves a bargain. Before facing the dealers, each seller has their item valued by auctioneer Simon Bower. Simon also gives them top tips on the history and key characteristics of their piece, so that when they enter the bidding room, they have all the information they need to try to haggle the best possible price from the dealers. All the dealers are spending their own money but have no idea what the sellers have brought in.

programme.title: Bridge of Lies
programme.desc: Ross Kemp presents the quiz show where a team of four – in this episode, friends Martin, Robyn, Paul and Wayne – take on the Bridge of Lies. One by one, they all face the Bridge, choosing who faces each crossing depending on the question category. Each crossing has 32 potential steps, including 22 truths and ten lies. They must cross the Bridge by stepping on the truths and avoiding the lies, earning money for each correct answer. Step on a lie and the Bridge will halve their money. Step on three lies, and they are out of the game. There is always a safe path across the Bridge. They just have to find it. Once they have each faced the Bridge on their own, those who have been successful will join forces to face the final crossing for a chance to take home the cash.

programme.title: Panorama
programme.desc: Whether you were wading through floods or struggling through a heatwave, 2026 was the year when you could hardly miss our extreme weather. Temperatures in the summer topped 30C for 33 days in a row. Months earlier, some parts of the UK saw 40 consecutive days of rain. The BBC's climate editor Justin Rowlatt investigates the impact of climate change on our weather. He speaks to scientists who warn that hotter summers and wetter winters are likely to become more typical, and looks at if enough is being done to adapt our towns and cities to the changing climate. Justin asks, as the cost of living continues to bite, are governments under pressure to ditch some green policies, or do they remain committed to tackling climate change?

programme.title: The Traitors Ireland
programme.desc: The doors of Slane Castle have opened once again, with 23 new players entering The Traitors Ireland for its second season. The line-up features contestants from across the country, ranging in age from 24 to 61 and including teachers, a postal worker, a psychotherapist, a musician, a stay-at-home dad, an Irish Defence Forces member, and an actor and drama teacher. Hosted once again by Siobhán McSweeney, the players attempt to navigate a game built on trust, strategy and deception, forming alliances while trying to work out who among them they can believe.

programme.title: Saturday Kitchen

programme.title: Simply Nigella
programme.desc: Packed with new recipes and tips designed to make our busy lives easier, Simply Nigella proves that whatever the occasion, food, in the eating and the making, should always be pleasurable. This episode is all about dishes that marry the comfort of the familiar with the freshness of the new, like Nigella's grown-up take on a family favourite - fluffy oat pancakes with a raspberry and honey syrup. For a fun lunch, there is a riff on the classic caesar salad. A casual supper with friends sees Nigella serving a green-inspired feast of squid and orzo pasta, complete with the Greek dessert of old rag pie - a sweet and savoury twist on a cheesecake. And finally, Nigella's take on a rice bowl with ginger, radish and avocado celebrates a few choice ingredients, resulting in a dish that is calming and uplifting to look at, as well as to eat.

programme.title: Bargain Hunt
programme.desc: Two teams of actors from Welsh language drama series Pobol y Cwm mark the show’s 50th birthday by battling it out in Builth Wells, with experts Kate Bliss and Izzie Balmer.

programme.title: The Football Interview
programme.desc: The Football Interview sees the biggest names in sport and entertainment join host Kelly Somers for bold, in-depth conversations about the nation’s favourite sport. We explore mindset and motivation, reflect on defining moments and career highs, and discuss personal insights. It’s a chance to show an honest, human and sometimes surprising side to familiar faces. At the heart of this is Kelly Somers – one of the most trusted, versatile and authentic voices in sports broadcasting. Kelly brings a brand of warmth and relatability that resonates with both athletes and audiences. What sets her apart is her ability to dig deeper with a sensitive approach, creating a space where athletes feel comfortable being open, honest and at times vulnerable. Each episode sees Kelly draw out stories and insight from the player behind the name about the beautiful game, their origins and values, and a look-ahead to the future from a sporting and personal perspective. She takes her subjects on a journey – and takes the viewer with her.

programme.desc: Linda makes a worrying discovery. Sharon and Eve strike up an unlikely friendship. Mark and Lauren struggle to find time.

programme.title: Panorama
programme.desc: Whether you were wading through floods or struggling through a heatwave, 2026 was the year when you could hardly miss our extreme weather. Temperatures in the summer topped 30C for 33 days in a row. Months earlier, some parts of the UK saw 40 consecutive days of rain. The BBC's climate editor Justin Rowlatt investigates the impact of climate change on our weather. He speaks to scientists who warn that hotter summers and wetter winters are likely to become more typical, and looks at if enough is being done to adapt our towns and cities to the changing climate. Justin asks, as the cost of living continues to bite, are governments under pressure to ditch some green policies, or do they remain committed to tackling climate change?

programme.title: This City Is Ours
programme.desc: The tragic events of the party send shock waves through the Phelans. As dangerous secrets threaten to come to light, Michael is forced to make a difficult confession to Diana. Meanwhile, unseen dangers close in, and it becomes clear no-one is safe.

programme.title: Simply Nigella
programme.desc: Packed with new recipes and tips designed to make our busy lives easier, Simply Nigella proves that whatever the occasion, food, in the eating and the making, should always be pleasurable. This episode is all about dishes that marry the comfort of the familiar with the freshness of the new, like Nigella's grown-up take on a family favourite - fluffy oat pancakes with a raspberry and honey syrup. For a fun lunch, there is a riff on the classic caesar salad. A casual supper with friends sees Nigella serving a green-inspired feast of squid and orzo pasta, complete with the Greek dessert of old rag pie - a sweet and savoury twist on a cheesecake. And finally, Nigella's take on a rice bowl with ginger, radish and avocado celebrates a few choice ingredients, resulting in a dish that is calming and uplifting to look at, as well as to eat.

programme.title: Bargain Hunt

programme.title: The Football Interview
programme.desc: The Football Interview sees the biggest names in sport and entertainment join host Kelly Somers for bold, in-depth conversations about the nation’s favourite sport. We explore mindset and motivation, reflect on defining moments and career highs, and discuss personal insights. It’s a chance to show an honest, human and sometimes surprising side to familiar faces. At the heart of this is Kelly Somers – one of the most trusted, versatile and authentic voices in sports broadcasting. Kelly brings a brand of warmth and relatability that resonates with both athletes and audiences. What sets her apart is her ability to dig deeper with a sensitive approach, creating a space where athletes feel comfortable being open, honest and at times vulnerable. Each episode sees Kelly draw out stories and insight from the player behind the name about the beautiful game, their origins and values, and a look-ahead to the future from a sporting and personal perspective. She takes her subjects on a journey – and takes the viewer with her.

programme.title: Remembrance Sunday: The Cenotaph
programme.desc: Sophie Raworth and Petroc Trelawny present live coverage from London as HM the King leads the Remembrance Sunday commemorations at the Cenotaph. His Majesty will be joined on Whitehall by senior members of the royal family and leading UK politicians, alongside representatives of the armed forces, the Commonwealth and faith communities for the two-minute silence at 11 o’clock and the National Service of Remembrance. This is followed by the annual wreath laying and the historic march past of 10,000 veterans as the nation remembers all those who have died serving their country. Accessible commentary and uninterrupted commentary-free coverage will be available on BBC iPlayer. A version with British Sign Language will also be available on Red Button and iPlayer.

programme.title: War Horse
programme.desc: Wartime drama. It is 1914, and struggling Devon farmer Ted Narracott buys a remarkable but unsuitable horse at auction. His son Albert names him Joey and, under pressure from their unscrupulous landlord, somehow trains Joey to work the farm. But when war breaks out, Joey is requisitioned by the army to serve at the front and begins a remarkable adventure that takes him far from Albert and the fields of Devon.

programme.title: Planet Earth Live
programme.desc: Sam, Sophie and Sybil are three tiny black bear cubs who have just emerged from their den in the Northwoods of Minnesota. But this spectacular wilderness is full of threats - wolves and coyotes roam the forest looking for stray cubs, the weather can be dangerously unpredictable bringing blizzards and forest fires, and every year, some of the black bears are killed by humans. Survival depends entirely on the experience of their mother and how well they learn the skills she teaches them. With the help of bear expert Dr Lynn Rogers, Julia Bradbury explores the woods, learning about the lives of the black bears and the particular trials facing these three vulnerable little cubs. Sam, Sophie and Sybil must follow their mother's lead closely if they are going to survive in this tough and unforgiving wilderness, and make it through this critical month.

programme.title: Blue Planet III
programme.desc: In the tropical seas, year-round sunshine has created the perfect conditions for the ocean’s richest habitats to flourish, but survival takes remarkable and surprising ingenuity.

programme.title: Countryfile
programme.desc: Figures for the first seven months of the year show milk production in Northern Ireland is heading for a record year. But fluctuating prices, rising costs and the ever-present threat of disease have left many dairy businesses under financial pressure. Alongside local farmer Emily McGowan, Charlotte Smith and Adam Henson explore how dairy farmers across County Antrim, one of Northern Ireland's most productive dairy regions, are turning to tech and innovative business models to build a more resilient future. Adam also introduces this year’s BBC Food and Farming Awards Countryfile Young Countryside Champion nominees.

programme.title: The Reluctant Vampire
programme.desc: The day of Val’s initiation ceremony approaches, and he still has no idea how he’ll pass the vampire test. When his final plan doesn’t work out, he realises he can no longer live a double life and is faced with the ultimate dilemma. Should he come clean and risk everything for the chance of a human life or sacrifice who he really is for the sake of his family?

programme.title: Strictly Come Dancing
programme.desc: It’s results time, and the couples wait to find out if they’ll be heading back to the training rooms to learn another new dance. programme.title: Dashcam Justice
programme.desc: A pedestrian hurls himself at a car, then blames the driver. But the dashcam reveals a murkier story. In Widnes, horse rider Jayne Scotson films a frighteningly close pass, while in Liverpool, a van mounts the pavement to dodge a bin lorry, and could take out innocent bystanders. Police and fraud investigators reveal how footage recorded by ordinary people helps them uncover the truth and pursue justice.

programme.title: Homes Under the Hammer
programme.desc: Dion time travels back to the 70s in Nottinghamshire, and it all feels very familiar. Martin is loving his surroundings in Bath, and Jacqui sees beyond the work that needs to be done in Norfolk to appreciate the potential.

programme.title: Bargain Hunt
programme.desc: Wooden shoe lasts are a common sight at antiques fairs, but do you know how they’re made? Natasha Raskin Sharp visits the workshop of cordwainer Payson Muller, originally a stonemason, who turned his talents to making bespoke shoes on hand-carved shoe lasts. He creates them from beech boughs before refining their shape using a knife and rasp. Hoping to cut a few deals of their own are two teams of bargain hunters, shopping for collectibles at Wetherby Racecourse. In blue are couple Martin and Nasreen, and their opponents are married duo Lisamarie and Jamie. Nasreen’s keen eye spots an ornate Russian caviar bowl and spoon, but the price tag is an eye-watering £600. Elsewhere, Jamie comes across a wacky glass vase that resembles a famous artist’s work, but Philip Serrell thinks it’s no masterpiece. At the sale, both teams hope for big profits, but all they can do is watch as their items go under auctioneer Caroline Hawley’s hammer.

programme.title: BBC News at One
programme.desc: The latest national and international news from the BBC.

programme.title: Money for Nothing
programme.desc: Jacqui Joseph is patrolling the forecourt of Altrincham recycling centre in Greater Manchester, hoping to find three items that are packed with potential and give them the chance to shine once more. She finds a pair of folding chairs, an old washstand and a collection of glass bottles. Upholsterer Simion Hawtin-Smith and upcycler Sarah Parmenter set to work helping Jacqui transform her finds, but will all three projects produce profits?

programme.title: Escape to the Country
programme.desc: Having spent many happy family holidays in Cornwall, a couple from Hertfordshire now want to make England’s most south-westerly county their permanent home, and Steve Brown is just the man to help them realise their dream. The trio also meet a local ceramicist and take part in a pottery throwdown.

programme.title: The Bidding Room
programme.desc: Nigel Havers presides as members of the public with interesting items to sell come face to face with five dealers who bid against each other to try to bag themselves a bargain. Before facing the dealers, each seller has their item valued by auctioneer Simon Bower. Simon also gives them top tips on the history and key characteristics of their piece, so that when they enter the bidding room, they have all the information they need to try to haggle the best possible price from the dealers. All the dealers are spending their own money but have no idea what the sellers have brought in.

programme.title: Bridge of Lies
programme.desc: Ross Kemp presents the quiz show where a team of four – in this episode, friends Martin, Robyn, Paul and Wayne – take on the Bridge of Lies. One by one, they all face the Bridge, choosing who faces each crossing depending on the question category. Each crossing has 32 potential steps, including 22 truths and ten lies. They must cross the Bridge by stepping on the truths and avoiding the lies, earning money for each correct answer. Step on a lie and the Bridge will halve their money. Step on three lies, and they are out of the game. There is always a safe path across the Bridge. They just have to find it. Once they have each faced the Bridge on their own, those who have been successful will join forces to face the final crossing for a chance to take home the cash.

programme.title: Pointless
programme.desc: Alexander Armstrong is joined by co-host Sally Phillips for the brainy quiz where the contestants try to score as few points as possible by plumbing the depths of their general knowledge to come up with the answers no-one else could think of.

programme.desc: Sam, Sophie and Sybil are three tiny black bear cubs who have just emerged from their den in the Northwoods of Minnesota. programme.title: Dashcam Justice
programme.desc: A pedestrian hurls himself at a car, then blames the driver. But the dashcam reveals a murkier story. In Widnes, horse rider Jayne Scotson films a frighteningly close pass, while in Liverpool, a van mounts the pavement to dodge a bin lorry, and could take out innocent bystanders. Police and fraud investigators reveal how footage recorded by ordinary people helps them uncover the truth and pursue justice.

programme.title: Homes Under the Hammer
programme.desc: Dion time travels back to the 70s in Nottinghamshire, and it all feels very familiar. Martin is loving his surroundings in Bath, and Jacqui sees beyond the work that needs to be done in Norfolk to appreciate the potential.

programme.title: Bargain Hunt
programme.desc: Wooden shoe lasts are a common sight at antiques fairs, but do you know how they’re made? Natasha Raskin Sharp visits the workshop of cordwainer Payson Muller, originally a stonemason, who turned his talents to making bespoke shoes on hand-carved shoe lasts. He creates them from beech boughs before refining their shape using a knife and rasp. Hoping to cut a few deals of their own are two teams of bargain hunters, shopping for collectibles at Wetherby Racecourse. In blue are couple Martin and Nasreen, and their opponents are married duo Lisamarie and Jamie. Nasreen’s keen eye spots an ornate Russian caviar bowl and spoon, but the price tag is an eye-watering £600. Elsewhere, Jamie comes across a wacky glass vase that resembles a famous artist’s work, but Philip Serrell thinks it’s no masterpiece. At the sale, both teams hope for big profits, but all they can do is watch as their items go under auctioneer Caroline Hawley’s hammer.

programme.title: Money for Nothing
programme.desc: Jacqui Joseph is patrolling the forecourt of Altrincham recycling centre in Greater Manchester, hoping to find three items that are packed with potential and give them the chance to shine once more. She finds a pair of folding chairs, an old washstand and a collection of glass bottles. Upholsterer Simion Hawtin-Smith and upcycler Sarah Parmenter set to work helping Jacqui transform her finds, but will all three projects produce profits?

programme.title: Escape to the Country
programme.desc: Having spent many happy family holidays in Cornwall, a couple from Hertfordshire now want to make England’s most south-westerly county their permanent home, and Steve Brown is just the man to help them realise their dream. The trio also meet a local ceramicist and take part in a pottery throwdown.

programme.title: The Bidding Room
programme.desc: Nigel Havers presides as members of the public with interesting items to sell come face to face with five dealers who bid against each other to try to bag themselves a bargain. Before facing the dealers, each seller has their item valued by auctioneer Simon Bower. Simon also gives them top tips on the history and key characteristics of their piece, so that when they enter the bidding room, they have all the information they need to try to haggle the best possible price from the dealers. All the dealers are spending their own money but have no idea what the sellers have brought in.

programme.title: Bridge of Lies
programme.desc: Ross Kemp presents the quiz show where a team of four – in this episode, friends Martin, Robyn, Paul and Wayne – take on the Bridge of Lies. One by one, they all face the Bridge, choosing who faces each crossing depending on the question category. Each crossing has 32 potential steps, including 22 truths and ten lies. They must cross the Bridge by stepping on the truths and avoiding the lies, earning money for each correct answer. Step on a lie and the Bridge will halve their money. Step on three lies, and they are out of the game. There is always a safe path across the Bridge. They just have to find it. Once they have each faced the Bridge on their own, those who have been successful will join forces to face the final crossing for a chance to take home the cash.

programme.title: Pointless
programme.desc: Alexander Armstrong is joined by co-host Sally Phillips for the brainy quiz where the contestants try to score as few points as possible by plumbing the depths of their general knowledge to come up with the answers no-one else could think of.

programme.title: Panorama
programme.desc: Whether you were wading through floods or struggling through a heatwave, 2026 was the year when you could hardly miss our extreme weather. Temperatures in the summer topped 30C for 33 days in a row. Months earlier, some parts of the UK saw 40 consecutive days of rain. The BBC's climate editor Justin Rowlatt investigates the impact of climate change on our weather. He speaks to scientists who warn that hotter summers and wetter winters are likely to become more typical, and looks at if enough is being done to adapt our towns and cities to the changing climate. Justin asks, as the cost of living continues to bite, are governments under pressure to ditch some green policies, or do they remain committed to tackling climate change?

programme.title: The Traitors Ireland
programme.desc: The doors of Slane Castle have opened once again, with 23 new players entering The Traitors Ireland for its second season. The line-up features contestants from across the country, ranging in age from 24 to 61 and including teachers, a postal worker, a psychotherapist, a musician, a stay-at-home dad, an Irish Defence Forces member, and an actor and drama teacher. Hosted once again by Siobhán McSweeney, the players attempt to navigate a game built on trust, strategy and deception, forming alliances while trying to work out who among them they can believe.

programme.title: Saturday Kitchen

programme.title: Simply Nigella
programme.desc: Packed with new recipes and tips designed to make our busy lives easier, Simply Nigella proves that whatever the occasion, food, in the eating and the making, should always be pleasurable. This episode is all about dishes that marry the comfort of the familiar with the freshness of the new, like Nigella's grown-up take on a family favourite - fluffy oat pancakes with a raspberry and honey syrup. For a fun lunch, there is a riff on the classic caesar salad. A casual supper with friends sees Nigella serving a green-inspired feast of squid and orzo pasta, complete with the Greek dessert of old rag pie - a sweet and savoury twist on a cheesecake. And finally, Nigella's take on a rice bowl with ginger, radish and avocado celebrates a few choice ingredients, resulting in a dish that is calming and uplifting to look at, as well as to eat.

programme.title: Bargain Hunt
programme.desc: Two teams of actors from Welsh language drama series Pobol y Cwm mark the show’s 50th birthday by battling it out in Builth Wells, with experts Kate Bliss and Izzie Balmer.

programme.title: The Football Interview
programme.desc: The Football Interview sees the biggest names in sport and entertainment join host Kelly Somers for bold, in-depth conversations about the nation’s favourite sport. We explore mindset and motivation, reflect on defining moments and career highs, and discuss personal insights. It’s a chance to show an honest, human and sometimes surprising side to familiar faces. At the heart of this is Kelly Somers – one of the most trusted, versatile and authentic voices in sports broadcasting. Kelly brings a brand of warmth and relatability that resonates with both athletes and audiences. What sets her apart is her ability to dig deeper with a sensitive approach, creating a space where athletes feel comfortable being open, honest and at times vulnerable. Each episode sees Kelly draw out stories and insight from the player behind the name about the beautiful game, their origins and values, and a look-ahead to the future from a sporting and personal perspective. She takes her subjects on a journey – and takes the viewer with her.

programme.desc: Whether you were wading through floods or struggling through a heatwave, 2026 was the year when you could hardly miss our extreme weather. programme.title: Simply Nigella
programme.desc: Packed with new recipes and tips designed to make our busy lives easier, Simply Nigella proves that whatever the occasion, food, in the eating and the making, should always be pleasurable. This episode is all about dishes that marry the comfort of the familiar with the freshness of the new, like Nigella's grown-up take on a family favourite - fluffy oat pancakes with a raspberry and honey syrup. For a fun lunch, there is a riff on the classic caesar salad. A casual supper with friends sees Nigella serving a green-inspired feast of squid and orzo pasta, complete with the Greek dessert of old rag pie - a sweet and savoury twist on a cheesecake. And finally, Nigella's take on a rice bowl with ginger, radish and avocado celebrates a few choice ingredients, resulting in a dish that is calming and uplifting to look at, as well as to eat.

programme.title: The Football Interview
programme.desc: The Football Interview sees the biggest names in sport and entertainment join host Kelly Somers for bold, in-depth conversations about the nation’s favourite sport. We explore mindset and motivation, reflect on defining moments and career highs, and discuss personal insights. It’s a chance to show an honest, human and sometimes surprising side to familiar faces. At the heart of this is Kelly Somers – one of the most trusted, versatile and authentic voices in sports broadcasting. Kelly brings a brand of warmth and relatability that resonates with both athletes and audiences. What sets her apart is her ability to dig deeper with a sensitive approach, creating a space where athletes feel comfortable being open, honest and at times vulnerable. Each episode sees Kelly draw out stories and insight from the player behind the name about the beautiful game, their origins and values, and a look-ahead to the future from a sporting and personal perspective. She takes her subjects on a journey – and takes the viewer with her.

programme.desc: Sophie Raworth and Petroc Trelawny present live coverage from London as HM the King leads the Remembrance Sunday commemorations at the Cenotaph. His Majesty will be joined on Whitehall by senior members of the royal family and leading UK politicians, alongside representatives of the armed forces, the Commonwealth and faith communities for the two-minute silence at 11 o’clock and the National Service of Remembrance. This is followed by the annual wreath laying and the historic march past of 10,000 veterans as the nation remembers all those who have died serving their country. programme.desc: Wartime drama. It is 1914, and struggling Devon farmer Ted Narracott buys a remarkable but unsuitable horse at auction. His son Albert names him Joey and, under pressure from their unscrupulous landlord, somehow trains Joey to work the farm. But when war breaks out, Joey is requisitioned by the army to serve at the front and begins a remarkable adventure that takes him far from Albert and the fields of Devon.

programme.title: Planet Earth Live
programme.desc: Sam, Sophie and Sybil are three tiny black bear cubs who have just emerged from their den in the Northwoods of Minnesota. But this spectacular wilderness is full of threats - wolves and coyotes roam the forest looking for stray cubs, the weather can be dangerously unpredictable bringing blizzards and forest fires, and every year, some of the black bears are killed by humans. Survival depends entirely on the experience of their mother and how well they learn the skills she teaches them. With the help of bear expert Dr Lynn Rogers, Julia Bradbury explores the woods, learning about the lives of the black bears and the particular trials facing these three vulnerable little cubs. Sam, Sophie and Sybil must follow their mother's lead closely if they are going to survive in this tough and unforgiving wilderness, and make it through this critical month.

programme.title: Oul Treasures
programme.desc: Presenter Lolly Spence continues the search for family heirlooms and prized possessions in desperate need of repair. Throughout the series, Lolly discovers what it takes to bring these items back to their former glory. Along the way, she meets some of the finest craftspeople in the country. This episode’s restoration brings Lolly to Carnalbanagh, an Ulster-Scots townland high in the hills of Co Antrim, where a lost record of community life has recently been uncovered. There could be absolute magic hidden in an old biscuit tin of films, and if there’s any chance of restoring them, Lolly’s going to need some very specialist help.

programme.title: Dashcam Justice
programme.desc: A pedestrian hurls himself at a car, then blames the driver. But the dashcam reveals a murkier story. In Widnes, horse rider Jayne Scotson films a frighteningly close pass, while in Liverpool, a van mounts the pavement to dodge a bin lorry, and could take out innocent bystanders. Police and fraud investigators reveal how footage recorded by ordinary people helps them uncover the truth and pursue justice.

programme.title: Homes Under the Hammer
programme.desc: Dion time travels back to the 70s in Nottinghamshire, and it all feels very familiar. Martin is loving his surroundings in Bath, and Jacqui sees beyond the work that needs to be done in Norfolk to appreciate the potential.

programme.title: Bargain Hunt
programme.desc: Wooden shoe lasts are a common sight at antiques fairs, but do you know how they’re made? Natasha Raskin Sharp visits the workshop of cordwainer Payson Muller, originally a stonemason, who turned his talents to making bespoke shoes on hand-carved shoe lasts. He creates them from beech boughs before refining their shape using a knife and rasp. Hoping to cut a few deals of their own are two teams of bargain hunters, shopping for collectibles at Wetherby Racecourse. In blue are couple Martin and Nasreen, and their opponents are married duo Lisamarie and Jamie. Nasreen’s keen eye spots an ornate Russian caviar bowl and spoon, but the price tag is an eye-watering £600. Elsewhere, Jamie comes across a wacky glass vase that resembles a famous artist’s work, but Philip Serrell thinks it’s no masterpiece. At the sale, both teams hope for big profits, but all they can do is watch as their items go under auctioneer Caroline Hawley’s hammer.

programme.desc: Jacqui Joseph is patrolling the forecourt of Altrincham recycling centre in Greater Manchester, hoping to find three items that are packed with potential and give them the chance to shine once more. She finds a pair of folding chairs, an old washstand and a collection of glass bottles. Upholsterer Simion Hawtin-Smith and upcycler Sarah Parmenter set to work helping Jacqui transform her finds, but will all three projects produce profits?

programme.title: Escape to the Country

The trio also meet a local ceramicist and take part in a pottery throwdown.

programme.title: The Bidding Room
programme.desc: Nigel Havers presides as members of the public with interesting items to sell come face to face with five dealers who bid against each other to try to bag themselves a bargain. Before facing the dealers, each seller has their item valued by auctioneer Simon Bower. Simon also gives them top tips on the history and key characteristics of their piece, so that when they enter the bidding room, they have all the information they need to try to haggle the best possible price from the dealers. All the dealers are spending their own money but have no idea what the sellers have brought in.

programme.title: Bridge of Lies
programme.desc: Ross Kemp presents the quiz show where a team of four – in this episode, friends Martin, Robyn, Paul and Wayne – take on the Bridge of Lies. One by one, they all face the Bridge, choosing who faces each crossing depending on the question category. Each crossing has 32 potential steps, including 22 truths and ten lies. They must cross the Bridge by stepping on the truths and avoiding the lies, earning money for each correct answer. Step on a lie and the Bridge will halve their money. Step on three lies, and they are out of the game. There is always a safe path across the Bridge. They just have to find it. Once they have each faced the Bridge on their own, those who have been successful will join forces to face the final crossing for a chance to take home the cash.

programme.title: War Horse
programme.desc: Wartime drama. It is 1914, and struggling Devon farmer Ted Narracott buys a remarkable but unsuitable horse at auction. His son Albert names him Joey and, under pressure from their unscrupulous landlord, somehow trains Joey to work the farm. But when war breaks out, Joey is requisitioned by the army to serve at the front and begins a remarkable adventure that takes him far from Albert and the fields of Devon.

programme.title: Planet Earth Live
programme.desc: Sam, Sophie and Sybil are three tiny black bear cubs who have just emerged from their den in the Northwoods of Minnesota. But this spectacular wilderness is full of threats - wolves and coyotes roam the forest looking for stray cubs, the weather can be dangerously unpredictable bringing blizzards and forest fires, and every year, some of the black bears are killed by humans. Survival depends entirely on the experience of their mother and how well they learn the skills she teaches them. With the help of bear expert Dr Lynn Rogers, Julia Bradbury explores the woods, learning about the lives of the black bears and the particular trials facing these three vulnerable little cubs. Sam, Sophie and Sybil must follow their mother's lead closely if they are going to survive in this tough and unforgiving wilderness, and make it through this critical month.

programme.desc: A pedestrian hurls himself at a car, then blames the driver. But the dashcam reveals a murkier story. In Widnes, horse rider Jayne Scotson films a frighteningly close pass, while in Liverpool, a van mounts the pavement to dodge a bin lorry, and could take out innocent bystanders. Police and fraud investigators reveal how footage recorded by ordinary people helps them uncover the truth and pursue justice.

programme.title: Homes Under the Hammer
programme.desc: Dion time travels back to the 70s in Nottinghamshire, and it all feels very familiar. Martin is loving his surroundings in Bath, and Jacqui sees beyond the work that needs to be done in Norfolk to appreciate the potential.

programme.title: Bargain Hunt
programme.desc: Wooden shoe lasts are a common sight at antiques fairs, but do you know how they’re made? Natasha Raskin Sharp visits the workshop of cordwainer Payson Muller, originally a stonemason, who turned his talents to making bespoke shoes on hand-carved shoe lasts. He creates them from beech boughs before refining their shape using a knife and rasp. Hoping to cut a few deals of their own are two teams of bargain hunters, shopping for collectibles at Wetherby Racecourse. In blue are couple Martin and Nasreen, and their opponents are married duo Lisamarie and Jamie. Nasreen’s keen eye spots an ornate Russian caviar bowl and spoon, but the price tag is an eye-watering £600. Elsewhere, Jamie comes across a wacky glass vase that resembles a famous artist’s work, but Philip Serrell thinks it’s no masterpiece. At the sale, both teams hope for big profits, but all they can do is watch as their items go under auctioneer Caroline Hawley’s hammer.

programme.title: BBC News at One
programme.desc: The latest national and international news from the BBC.

programme.title: Money for Nothing
programme.desc: Jacqui Joseph is patrolling the forecourt of Altrincham recycling centre in Greater Manchester, hoping to find three items that are packed with potential and give them the chance to shine once more. She finds a pair of folding chairs, an old washstand and a collection of glass bottles. Upholsterer Simion Hawtin-Smith and upcycler Sarah Parmenter set to work helping Jacqui transform her finds, but will all three projects produce profits?

programme.title: Escape to the Country
programme.desc: Having spent many happy family holidays in Cornwall, a couple from Hertfordshire now want to make England’s most south-westerly county their permanent home, and Steve Brown is just the man to help them realise their dream. The trio also meet a local ceramicist and take part in a pottery throwdown.

programme.title: The Bidding Room
programme.desc: Nigel Havers presides as members of the public with interesting items to sell come face to face with five dealers who bid against each other to try to bag themselves a bargain. Before facing the dealers, each seller has their item valued by auctioneer Simon Bower. Simon also gives them top tips on the history and key characteristics of their piece, so that when they enter the bidding room, they have all the information they need to try to haggle the best possible price from the dealers. All the dealers are spending their own money but have no idea what the sellers have brought in.

programme.title: Bridge of Lies
programme.desc: Ross Kemp presents the quiz show where a team of four – in this episode, friends Martin, Robyn, Paul and Wayne – take on the Bridge of Lies. One by one, they all face the Bridge, choosing who faces each crossing depending on the question category. Each crossing has 32 potential steps, including 22 truths and ten lies. They must cross the Bridge by stepping on the truths and avoiding the lies, earning money for each correct answer. Step on a lie and the Bridge will halve their money. Step on three lies, and they are out of the game. There is always a safe path across the Bridge. They just have to find it. Once they have each faced the Bridge on their own, those who have been successful will join forces to face the final crossing for a chance to take home the cash.

programme.title: Pointless
programme.desc: Alexander Armstrong is joined by co-host Sally Phillips for the brainy quiz where the contestants try to score as few points as possible by plumbing the depths of their general knowledge to come up with the answers no-one else could think of.

programme.title: Panorama
programme.desc: Whether you were wading through floods or struggling through a heatwave, 2026 was the year when you could hardly miss our extreme weather. Temperatures in the summer topped 30C for 33 days in a row. Months earlier, some parts of the UK saw 40 consecutive days of rain. The BBC's climate editor Justin Rowlatt investigates the impact of climate change on our weather. He speaks to scientists who warn that hotter summers and wetter winters are likely to become more typical, and looks at if enough is being done to adapt our towns and cities to the changing climate. Justin asks, as the cost of living continues to bite, are governments under pressure to ditch some green policies, or do they remain committed to tackling climate change?

programme.desc: Matt Tebbutt is joined by chefs Vivek Singh, Tom Parker Bowles and Riya Patel, and by special guest Jo Brand. Drinks expert Helen McGinn picks the wines to go with the studio dishes, and there are also great moments from the BBC food archive.

programme.title: Simply Nigella
programme.desc: Packed with new recipes and tips designed to make our busy lives easier, Simply Nigella proves that whatever the occasion, food, in the eating and the making, should always be pleasurable. This episode is all about dishes that marry the comfort of the familiar with the freshness of the new, like Nigella's grown-up take on a family favourite - fluffy oat pancakes with a raspberry and honey syrup. For a fun lunch, there is a riff on the classic caesar salad. A casual supper with friends sees Nigella serving a green-inspired feast of squid and orzo pasta, complete with the Greek dessert of old rag pie - a sweet and savoury twist on a cheesecake. And finally, Nigella's take on a rice bowl with ginger, radish and avocado celebrates a few choice ingredients, resulting in a dish that is calming and uplifting to look at, as well as to eat.

programme.title: Bargain Hunt
programme.desc: Two teams of actors from Welsh language drama series Pobol y Cwm mark the show’s 50th birthday by battling it out in Builth Wells, with experts Kate Bliss and Izzie Balmer.

programme.title: The Football Interview
programme.desc: The Football Interview sees the biggest names in sport and entertainment join host Kelly Somers for bold, in-depth conversations about the nation’s favourite sport. We explore mindset and motivation, reflect on defining moments and career highs, and discuss personal insights. It’s a chance to show an honest, human and sometimes surprising side to familiar faces. At the heart of this is Kelly Somers – one of the most trusted, versatile and authentic voices in sports broadcasting. Kelly brings a brand of warmth and relatability that resonates with both athletes and audiences. What sets her apart is her ability to dig deeper with a sensitive approach, creating a space where athletes feel comfortable being open, honest and at times vulnerable. Each episode sees Kelly draw out stories and insight from the player behind the name about the beautiful game, their origins and values, and a look-ahead to the future from a sporting and personal perspective. She takes her subjects on a journey – and takes the viewer with her.

programme.desc: Jacqui Joseph is patrolling the forecourt of Altrincham recycling centre in Greater Manchester, hoping to find three items that are packed with potential and give them the chance to shine once more. She finds a pair of folding chairs, an old washstand and a collection of glass bottles. Upholsterer Simion Hawtin-Smith and upcycler Sarah Parmenter set to work helping Jacqui transform her finds, but will all three projects produce profits?

programme.title: Escape to the Country
programme.desc: Having spent many happy family holidays in Cornwall, a couple from Hertfordshire now want to make England’s most south-westerly county their permanent home, and Steve Brown is just the man to help them realise their dream. The trio also meet a local ceramicist and take part in a pottery throwdown.

programme.title: The Bidding Room
programme.desc: Nigel Havers presides as members of the public with interesting items to sell come face to face with five dealers who bid against each other to try to bag themselves a bargain. Before facing the dealers, each seller has their item valued by auctioneer Simon Bower. Simon also gives them top tips on the history and key characteristics of their piece, so that when they enter the bidding room, they have all the information they need to try to haggle the best possible price from the dealers. All the dealers are spending their own money but have no idea what the sellers have brought in.

programme.title: Bridge of Lies
programme.desc: Ross Kemp presents the quiz show where a team of four – in this episode, friends Martin, Robyn, Paul and Wayne – take on the Bridge of Lies. One by one, they all face the Bridge, choosing who faces each crossing depending on the question category. Each crossing has 32 potential steps, including 22 truths and ten lies. They must cross the Bridge by stepping on the truths and avoiding the lies, earning money for each correct answer. Step on a lie and the Bridge will halve their money. Step on three lies, and they are out of the game. There is always a safe path across the Bridge. They just have to find it. Once they have each faced the Bridge on their own, those who have been successful will join forces to face the final crossing for a chance to take home the cash.

programme.title: Panorama
programme.desc: Whether you were wading through floods or struggling through a heatwave, 2026 was the year when you could hardly miss our extreme weather. Temperatures in the summer topped 30C for 33 days in a row. Months earlier, some parts of the UK saw 40 consecutive days of rain. The BBC's climate editor Justin Rowlatt investigates the impact of climate change on our weather. He speaks to scientists who warn that hotter summers and wetter winters are likely to become more typical, and looks at if enough is being done to adapt our towns and cities to the changing climate. Justin asks, as the cost of living continues to bite, are governments under pressure to ditch some green policies, or do they remain committed to tackling climate change?

programme.title: Simply Nigella
programme.desc: Packed with new recipes and tips designed to make our busy lives easier, Simply Nigella proves that whatever the occasion, food, in the eating and the making, should always be pleasurable. This episode is all about dishes that marry the comfort of the familiar with the freshness of the new, like Nigella's grown-up take on a family favourite - fluffy oat pancakes with a raspberry and honey syrup. For a fun lunch, there is a riff on the classic caesar salad. A casual supper with friends sees Nigella serving a green-inspired feast of squid and orzo pasta, complete with the Greek dessert of old rag pie - a sweet and savoury twist on a cheesecake. And finally, Nigella's take on a rice bowl with ginger, radish and avocado celebrates a few choice ingredients, resulting in a dish that is calming and uplifting to look at, as well as to eat.

programme.title: Bargain Hunt
programme.desc: Two teams of actors from Welsh language drama series Pobol y Cwm mark the show’s 50th birthday by battling it out in Builth Wells, with experts Kate Bliss and Izzie Balmer.

programme.title: The Football Interview
programme.desc: The Football Interview sees the biggest names in sport and entertainment join host Kelly Somers for bold, in-depth conversations about the nation’s favourite sport. We explore mindset and motivation, reflect on defining moments and career highs, and discuss personal insights. It’s a chance to show an honest, human and sometimes surprising side to familiar faces. At the heart of this is Kelly Somers – one of the most trusted, versatile and authentic voices in sports broadcasting. Kelly brings a brand of warmth and relatability that resonates with both athletes and audiences. What sets her apart is her ability to dig deeper with a sensitive approach, creating a space where athletes feel comfortable being open, honest and at times vulnerable. Each episode sees Kelly draw out stories and insight from the player behind the name about the beautiful game, their origins and values, and a look-ahead to the future from a sporting and personal perspective. She takes her subjects on a journey – and takes the viewer with her.

programme.title: Remembrance Sunday: The Cenotaph
programme.desc: Sophie Raworth and Petroc Trelawny present live coverage from London as HM the King leads the Remembrance Sunday commemorations at the Cenotaph. His Majesty will be joined on Whitehall by senior members of the royal family and leading UK politicians, alongside representatives of the armed forces, the Commonwealth and faith communities for the two-minute silence at 11 o’clock and the National Service of Remembrance. This is followed by the annual wreath laying and the historic march past of 10,000 veterans as the nation remembers all those who have died serving their country. Accessible commentary and uninterrupted commentary-free coverage will be available on BBC iPlayer. A version with British Sign Language will also be available on Red Button and iPlayer.

programme.title: War Horse
programme.desc: Wartime drama. It is 1914, and struggling Devon farmer Ted Narracott buys a remarkable but unsuitable horse at auction. His son Albert names him Joey and, under pressure from their unscrupulous landlord, somehow trains Joey to work the farm. But when war breaks out, Joey is requisitioned by the army to serve at the front and begins a remarkable adventure that takes him far from Albert and the fields of Devon.

programme.title: Planet Earth Live
programme.desc: Sam, Sophie and Sybil are three tiny black bear cubs who have just emerged from their den in the Northwoods of Minnesota. But this spectacular wilderness is full of threats - wolves and coyotes roam the forest looking for stray cubs, the weather can be dangerously unpredictable bringing blizzards and forest fires, and every year, some of the black bears are killed by humans. Survival depends entirely on the experience of their mother and how well they learn the skills she teaches them. With the help of bear expert Dr Lynn Rogers, Julia Bradbury explores the woods, learning about the lives of the black bears and the particular trials facing these three vulnerable little cubs. Sam, Sophie and Sybil must follow their mother's lead closely if they are going to survive in this tough and unforgiving wilderness, and make it through this critical month.

programme.title: Countryfile
programme.desc: Figures for the first seven months of the year show milk production in Northern Ireland is heading for a record year. Adam also introduces this year’s BBC Food and Farming Awards Countryfile Young Countryside Champion nominees.

programme.desc: A pedestrian hurls himself at a car, then blames the driver. But the dashcam reveals a murkier story. In Widnes, horse rider Jayne Scotson films a frighteningly close pass, while in Liverpool, a van mounts the pavement to dodge a bin lorry, and could take out innocent bystanders. Police and fraud investigators reveal how footage recorded by ordinary people helps them uncover the truth and pursue justice.

programme.title: Homes Under the Hammer
programme.desc: Dion time travels back to the 70s in Nottinghamshire, and it all feels very familiar. Martin is loving his surroundings in Bath, and Jacqui sees beyond the work that needs to be done in Norfolk to appreciate the potential.

programme.title: Bargain Hunt
programme.desc: Wooden shoe lasts are a common sight at antiques fairs, but do you know how they’re made? Natasha Raskin Sharp visits the workshop of cordwainer Payson Muller, originally a stonemason, who turned his talents to making bespoke shoes on hand-carved shoe lasts. He creates them from beech boughs before refining their shape using a knife and rasp. Hoping to cut a few deals of their own are two teams of bargain hunters, shopping for collectibles at Wetherby Racecourse. In blue are couple Martin and Nasreen, and their opponents are married duo Lisamarie and Jamie. Nasreen’s keen eye spots an ornate Russian caviar bowl and spoon, but the price tag is an eye-watering £600. Elsewhere, Jamie comes across a wacky glass vase that resembles a famous artist’s work, but Philip Serrell thinks it’s no masterpiece. At the sale, both teams hope for big profits, but all they can do is watch as their items go under auctioneer Caroline Hawley’s hammer.

programme.title: War Horse
programme.desc: Wartime drama. It is 1914, and struggling Devon farmer Ted Narracott buys a remarkable but unsuitable horse at auction. His son Albert names him Joey and, under pressure from their unscrupulous landlord, somehow trains Joey to work the farm. But when war breaks out, Joey is requisitioned by the army to serve at the front and begins a remarkable adventure that takes him far from Albert and the fields of Devon.

programme.title: Planet Earth Live
programme.desc: Sam, Sophie and Sybil are three tiny black bear cubs who have just emerged from their den in the Northwoods of Minnesota. But this spectacular wilderness is full of threats - wolves and coyotes roam the forest looking for stray cubs, the weather can be dangerously unpredictable bringing blizzards and forest fires, and every year, some of the black bears are killed by humans. Survival depends entirely on the experience of their mother and how well they learn the skills she teaches them. With the help of bear expert Dr Lynn Rogers, Julia Bradbury explores the woods, learning about the lives of the black bears and the particular trials facing these three vulnerable little cubs. Sam, Sophie and Sybil must follow their mother's lead closely if they are going to survive in this tough and unforgiving wilderness, and make it through this critical month.

programme.title: Blue Planet III
programme.desc: In the tropical seas, year-round sunshine has created the perfect conditions for the ocean’s richest habitats to flourish, but survival takes remarkable and surprising ingenuity.

programme.title: Dashcam Justice
programme.desc: A pedestrian hurls himself at a car, then blames the driver. But the dashcam reveals a murkier story. In Widnes, horse rider Jayne Scotson films a frighteningly close pass, while in Liverpool, a van mounts the pavement to dodge a bin lorry, and could take out innocent bystanders. Police and fraud investigators reveal how footage recorded by ordinary people helps them uncover the truth and pursue justice.

programme.title: Homes Under the Hammer
programme.desc: Dion time travels back to the 70s in Nottinghamshire, and it all feels very familiar. Martin is loving his surroundings in Bath, and Jacqui sees beyond the work that needs to be done in Norfolk to appreciate the potential.

programme.title: Bargain Hunt
programme.desc: Wooden shoe lasts are a common sight at antiques fairs, but do you know how they’re made? Natasha Raskin Sharp visits the workshop of cordwainer Payson Muller, originally a stonemason, who turned his talents to making bespoke shoes on hand-carved shoe lasts. He creates them from beech boughs before refining their shape using a knife and rasp. Hoping to cut a few deals of their own are two teams of bargain hunters, shopping for collectibles at Wetherby Racecourse. In blue are couple Martin and Nasreen, and their opponents are married duo Lisamarie and Jamie. Nasreen’s keen eye spots an ornate Russian caviar bowl and spoon, but the price tag is an eye-watering £600. Elsewhere, Jamie comes across a wacky glass vase that resembles a famous artist’s work, but Philip Serrell thinks it’s no masterpiece. At the sale, both teams hope for big profits, but all they can do is watch as their items go under auctioneer Caroline Hawley’s hammer.

programme.title: BBC News at One
programme.desc: The latest national and international news from the BBC.

programme.title: Money for Nothing
programme.desc: Jacqui Joseph is patrolling the forecourt of Altrincham recycling centre in Greater Manchester, hoping to find three items that are packed with potential and give them the chance to shine once more. She finds a pair of folding chairs, an old washstand and a collection of glass bottles. Upholsterer Simion Hawtin-Smith and upcycler Sarah Parmenter set to work helping Jacqui transform her finds, but will all three projects produce profits?

programme.title: Escape to the Country
programme.desc: Having spent many happy family holidays in Cornwall, a couple from Hertfordshire now want to make England’s most south-westerly county their permanent home, and Steve Brown is just the man to help them realise their dream. The trio also meet a local ceramicist and take part in a pottery throwdown.

programme.title: The Bidding Room
programme.desc: Nigel Havers presides as members of the public with interesting items to sell come face to face with five dealers who bid against each other to try to bag themselves a bargain. Before facing the dealers, each seller has their item valued by auctioneer Simon Bower. Simon also gives them top tips on the history and key characteristics of their piece, so that when they enter the bidding room, they have all the information they need to try to haggle the best possible price from the dealers. All the dealers are spending their own money but have no idea what the sellers have brought in.

programme.title: Bridge of Lies
programme.desc: Ross Kemp presents the quiz show where a team of four – in this episode, friends Martin, Robyn, Paul and Wayne – take on the Bridge of Lies. One by one, they all face the Bridge, choosing who faces each crossing depending on the question category. Each crossing has 32 potential steps, including 22 truths and ten lies. They must cross the Bridge by stepping on the truths and avoiding the lies, earning money for each correct answer. Step on a lie and the Bridge will halve their money. Step on three lies, and they are out of the game. There is always a safe path across the Bridge. They just have to find it. Once they have each faced the Bridge on their own, those who have been successful will join forces to face the final crossing for a chance to take home the cash.

programme.title: Pointless
programme.desc: Alexander Armstrong is joined by co-host Sally Phillips for the brainy quiz where the contestants try to score as few points as possible by plumbing the depths of their general knowledge to come up with the answers no-one else could think of.

programme.title: EastEnders
programme.desc: Linda makes a worrying discovery. Sharon and Eve strike up an unlikely friendship. Mark and Lauren struggle to find time.

programme.title: Panorama
programme.desc: Whether you were wading through floods or struggling through a heatwave, 2026 was the year when you could hardly miss our extreme weather. Temperatures in the summer topped 30C for 33 days in a row. Months earlier, some parts of the UK saw 40 consecutive days of rain. The BBC's climate editor Justin Rowlatt investigates the impact of climate change on our weather. He speaks to scientists who warn that hotter summers and wetter winters are likely to become more typical, and looks at if enough is being done to adapt our towns and cities to the changing climate. Justin asks, as the cost of living continues to bite, are governments under pressure to ditch some green policies, or do they remain committed to tackling climate change?

programme.title: This City Is Ours
programme.desc: The tragic events of the party send shock waves through the Phelans. As dangerous secrets threaten to come to light, Michael is forced to make a difficult confession to Diana. Meanwhile, unseen dangers close in, and it becomes clear no-one is safe.

programme.desc: The latest national and international news, with reports from BBC correspondents worldwide.

programme.title: Spotlight
programme.desc: The latest news, sport, weather and features from the South West of England.

programme.title: Have I Got News for You
programme.desc: Steph McGovern hosts, with guest panellists journalist Helen Lewis and comedian and actor John Tothill joining team captains Ian Hislop and Paul Merton as they delve into the news.

programme.title: The Traitors Ireland
programme.desc: The doors of Slane Castle have opened once again, with 23 new players entering The Traitors Ireland for its second season. The line-up features contestants from across the country, ranging in age from 24 to 61 and including teachers, a postal worker, a psychotherapist, a musician, a stay-at-home dad, an Irish Defence Forces member, and an actor and drama teacher. Hosted once again by Siobhán McSweeney, the players attempt to navigate a game built on trust, strategy and deception, forming alliances while trying to work out who among them they can believe.

programme.title: RuPaul's Drag Race UK
programme.desc: It’s the grand finale! The time has come for the competition to conclude as the queens compete in their final challenge - an all-singing, all-dancing extravaganza to fight for the crown. Choreographer Claudimar Neto coaches the queens as they perform a megamix of Drag Race UK’s most iconic girl group songs. As ever, it’s a family line-up for the finale, with Michelle Visage, Alan Carr and Graham Norton forming the judging panel, while last year’s winner and reigning champion Bones drops by along with this season’s eliminated queens. Everyone’s back to witness RuPaul crown the UK’s Next Drag Race Superstar.

programme.title: Saturday Kitchen
programme.desc: Matt Tebbutt is joined by chefs Vivek Singh, Tom Parker Bowles and Riya Patel, and by special guest Jo Brand. Drinks expert Helen McGinn picks the wines to go with the studio dishes, and there are also great moments from the BBC food archive.

programme.title: Simply Nigella
programme.desc: Packed with new recipes and tips designed to make our busy lives easier, Simply Nigella proves that whatever the occasion, food, in the eating and the making, should always be pleasurable. This episode is all about dishes that marry the comfort of the familiar with the freshness of the new, like Nigella's grown-up take on a family favourite - fluffy oat pancakes with a raspberry and honey syrup. For a fun lunch, there is a riff on the classic caesar salad. A casual supper with friends sees Nigella serving a green-inspired feast of squid and orzo pasta, complete with the Greek dessert of old rag pie - a sweet and savoury twist on a cheesecake. And finally, Nigella's take on a rice bowl with ginger, radish and avocado celebrates a few choice ingredients, resulting in a dish that is calming and uplifting to look at, as well as to eat.

programme.title: Bargain Hunt
programme.desc: Two teams of actors from Welsh language drama series Pobol y Cwm mark the show’s 50th birthday by battling it out in Builth Wells, with experts Kate Bliss and Izzie Balmer.

programme.title: The Football Interview
programme.desc: The Football Interview sees the biggest names in sport and entertainment join host Kelly Somers for bold, in-depth conversations about the nation’s favourite sport. We explore mindset and motivation, reflect on defining moments and career highs, and discuss personal insights. It’s a chance to show an honest, human and sometimes surprising side to familiar faces. At the heart of this is Kelly Somers – one of the most trusted, versatile and authentic voices in sports broadcasting. Kelly brings a brand of warmth and relatability that resonates with both athletes and audiences. What sets her apart is her ability to dig deeper with a sensitive approach, creating a space where athletes feel comfortable being open, honest and at times vulnerable. Each episode sees Kelly draw out stories and insight from the player behind the name about the beautiful game, their origins and values, and a look-ahead to the future from a sporting and personal perspective. She takes her subjects on a journey – and takes the viewer with her.

programme.desc: Wooden shoe lasts are a common sight at antiques fairs, but do you know how they’re made? Natasha Raskin Sharp visits the workshop of cordwainer Payson Muller, originally a stonemason, who turned his talents to making bespoke shoes on hand-carved shoe lasts. He creates them from beech boughs before refining their shape using a knife and rasp. Hoping to cut a few deals of their own are two teams of bargain hunters, shopping for collectibles at Wetherby Racecourse. In blue are couple Martin and Nasreen, and their opponents are married duo Lisamarie and Jamie. Nasreen’s keen eye spots an ornate Russian caviar bowl and spoon, but the price tag is an eye-watering £600. Elsewhere, Jamie comes across a wacky glass vase that resembles a famous artist’s work, but Philip Serrell thinks it’s no masterpiece. At the sale, both teams hope for big profits, but all they can do is watch as their items go under auctioneer Caroline Hawley’s hammer.

programme.title: Bridge of Lies
programme.desc: Ross Kemp presents the quiz show where a team of four – in this episode, friends Martin, Robyn, Paul and Wayne – take on the Bridge of Lies. One by one, they all face the Bridge, choosing who faces each crossing depending on the question category. Each crossing has 32 potential steps, including 22 truths and ten lies. They must cross the Bridge by stepping on the truths and avoiding the lies, earning money for each correct answer. Step on a lie and the Bridge will halve their money. Step on three lies, and they are out of the game. There is always a safe path across the Bridge. They just have to find it. Once they have each faced the Bridge on their own, those who have been successful will join forces to face the final crossing for a chance to take home the cash.

programme.title: Panorama
programme.desc: Whether you were wading through floods or struggling through a heatwave, 2026 was the year when you could hardly miss our extreme weather. Temperatures in the summer topped 30C for 33 days in a row. Months earlier, some parts of the UK saw 40 consecutive days of rain. The BBC's climate editor Justin Rowlatt investigates the impact of climate change on our weather. He speaks to scientists who warn that hotter summers and wetter winters are likely to become more typical, and looks at if enough is being done to adapt our towns and cities to the changing climate. Justin asks, as the cost of living continues to bite, are governments under pressure to ditch some green policies, or do they remain committed to tackling climate change?

programme.title: The Traitors Ireland
programme.desc: The doors of Slane Castle have opened once again, with 23 new players entering The Traitors Ireland for its second season. The line-up features contestants from across the country, ranging in age from 24 to 61 and including teachers, a postal worker, a psychotherapist, a musician, a stay-at-home dad, an Irish Defence Forces member, and an actor and drama teacher. Hosted once again by Siobhán McSweeney, the players attempt to navigate a game built on trust, strategy and deception, forming alliances while trying to work out who among them they can believe.

programme.title: Simply Nigella
programme.desc: Packed with new recipes and tips designed to make our busy lives easier, Simply Nigella proves that whatever the occasion, food, in the eating and the making, should always be pleasurable. This episode is all about dishes that marry the comfort of the familiar with the freshness of the new, like Nigella's grown-up take on a family favourite - fluffy oat pancakes with a raspberry and honey syrup. For a fun lunch, there is a riff on the classic caesar salad. A casual supper with friends sees Nigella serving a green-inspired feast of squid and orzo pasta, complete with the Greek dessert of old rag pie - a sweet and savoury twist on a cheesecake. And finally, Nigella's take on a rice bowl with ginger, radish and avocado celebrates a few choice ingredients, resulting in a dish that is calming and uplifting to look at, as well as to eat.

programme.title: Bargain Hunt
programme.desc: Two teams of actors from Welsh language drama series Pobol y Cwm mark the show’s 50th birthday by battling it out in Builth Wells, with experts Kate Bliss and Izzie Balmer.

programme.title: The Football Interview
programme.desc: The Football Interview sees the biggest names in sport and entertainment join host Kelly Somers for bold, in-depth conversations about the nation’s favourite sport. We explore mindset and motivation, reflect on defining moments and career highs, and discuss personal insights. It’s a chance to show an honest, human and sometimes surprising side to familiar faces. At the heart of this is Kelly Somers – one of the most trusted, versatile and authentic voices in sports broadcasting. Kelly brings a brand of warmth and relatability that resonates with both athletes and audiences. What sets her apart is her ability to dig deeper with a sensitive approach, creating a space where athletes feel comfortable being open, honest and at times vulnerable. Each episode sees Kelly draw out stories and insight from the player behind the name about the beautiful game, their origins and values, and a look-ahead to the future from a sporting and personal perspective. She takes her subjects on a journey – and takes the viewer with her.

programme.title: Remembrance Sunday: The Cenotaph
programme.desc: Sophie Raworth and Petroc Trelawny present live coverage from London as HM the King leads the Remembrance Sunday commemorations at the Cenotaph. His Majesty will be joined on Whitehall by senior members of the royal family and leading UK politicians, alongside representatives of the armed forces, the Commonwealth and faith communities for the two-minute silence at 11 o’clock and the National Service of Remembrance. This is followed by the annual wreath laying and the historic march past of 10,000 veterans as the nation remembers all those who have died serving their country. Accessible commentary and uninterrupted commentary-free coverage will be available on BBC iPlayer. A version with British Sign Language will also be available on Red Button and iPlayer.

programme.title: War Horse
programme.desc: Wartime drama. It is 1914, and struggling Devon farmer Ted Narracott buys a remarkable but unsuitable horse at auction. His son Albert names him Joey and, under pressure from their unscrupulous landlord, somehow trains Joey to work the farm. But when war breaks out, Joey is requisitioned by the army to serve at the front and begins a remarkable adventure that takes him far from Albert and the fields of Devon.

programme.title: Planet Earth Live
programme.desc: Sam, Sophie and Sybil are three tiny black bear cubs who have just emerged from their den in the Northwoods of Minnesota. But this spectacular wilderness is full of threats - wolves and coyotes roam the forest looking for stray cubs, the weather can be dangerously unpredictable bringing blizzards and forest fires, and every year, some of the black bears are killed by humans. Survival depends entirely on the experience of their mother and how well they learn the skills she teaches them. With the help of bear expert Dr Lynn Rogers, Julia Bradbury explores the woods, learning about the lives of the black bears and the particular trials facing these three vulnerable little cubs. Sam, Sophie and Sybil must follow their mother's lead closely if they are going to survive in this tough and unforgiving wilderness, and make it through this critical month.

The presenters walk alongside five remarkable young people who have faced significant challenges, hearing first-hand how BBC Children in Need-funded projects have helped them build confidence, resilience and hope for the future.

programme.title: Remembrance Sunday: The Cenotaph
programme.desc: Sophie Raworth and Petroc Trelawny present live coverage from London as HM the King leads the Remembrance Sunday commemorations at the Cenotaph. His Majesty will be joined on Whitehall by senior members of the royal family and leading UK politicians, alongside representatives of the armed forces, the Commonwealth and faith communities for the two-minute silence at 11 o’clock and the National Service of Remembrance. This is followed by the annual wreath laying and the historic march past of 10,000 veterans as the nation remembers all those who have died serving their country. Accessible commentary and uninterrupted commentary-free coverage will be available on BBC iPlayer. A version with British Sign Language will also be available on Red Button and iPlayer.

programme.title: War Horse
programme.desc: Wartime drama. It is 1914, and struggling Devon farmer Ted Narracott buys a remarkable but unsuitable horse at auction. His son Albert names him Joey and, under pressure from their unscrupulous landlord, somehow trains Joey to work the farm. But when war breaks out, Joey is requisitioned by the army to serve at the front and begins a remarkable adventure that takes him far from Albert and the fields of Devon.

programme.title: Planet Earth Live
programme.desc: Sam, Sophie and Sybil are three tiny black bear cubs who have just emerged from their den in the Northwoods of Minnesota. But this spectacular wilderness is full of threats - wolves and coyotes roam the forest looking for stray cubs, the weather can be dangerously unpredictable bringing blizzards and forest fires, and every year, some of the black bears are killed by humans. Survival depends entirely on the experience of their mother and how well they learn the skills she teaches them. With the help of bear expert Dr Lynn Rogers, Julia Bradbury explores the woods, learning about the lives of the black bears and the particular trials facing these three vulnerable little cubs. Sam, Sophie and Sybil must follow their mother's lead closely if they are going to survive in this tough and unforgiving wilderness, and make it through this critical month.

programme.title: Countryfile
programme.desc: Figures for the first seven months of the year show milk production in Northern Ireland is heading for a record year. But fluctuating prices, rising costs and the ever-present threat of disease have left many dairy businesses under financial pressure. Alongside local farmer Emily McGowan, Charlotte Smith and Adam Henson explore how dairy farmers across County Antrim, one of Northern Ireland's most productive dairy regions, are turning to tech and innovative business models to build a more resilient future. Adam also introduces this year’s BBC Food and Farming Awards Countryfile Young Countryside Champion nominees.

programme.title: The Reluctant Vampire
programme.desc: The day of Val’s initiation ceremony approaches, and he still has no idea how he’ll pass the vampire test. Should he come clean and risk everything for the chance of a human life or sacrifice who he really is for the sake of his family?

Two couples will find themselves in the dance-off, competing for the one remaining place in the next show. Who will the judges decide should keep dancing?

programme.title: Dashcam Justice
programme.desc: A pedestrian hurls himself at a car, then blames the driver. But the dashcam reveals a murkier story. In Widnes, horse rider Jayne Scotson films a frighteningly close pass, while in Liverpool, a van mounts the pavement to dodge a bin lorry, and could take out innocent bystanders. Police and fraud investigators reveal how footage recorded by ordinary people helps them uncover the truth and pursue justice.

programme.title: Homes Under the Hammer
programme.desc: Dion time travels back to the 70s in Nottinghamshire, and it all feels very familiar. Martin is loving his surroundings in Bath, and Jacqui sees beyond the work that needs to be done in Norfolk to appreciate the potential.

programme.title: Bargain Hunt
programme.desc: Wooden shoe lasts are a common sight at antiques fairs, but do you know how they’re made? Natasha Raskin Sharp visits the workshop of cordwainer Payson Muller, originally a stonemason, who turned his talents to making bespoke shoes on hand-carved shoe lasts. He creates them from beech boughs before refining their shape using a knife and rasp. Hoping to cut a few deals of their own are two teams of bargain hunters, shopping for collectibles at Wetherby Racecourse. In blue are couple Martin and Nasreen, and their opponents are married duo Lisamarie and Jamie. Nasreen’s keen eye spots an ornate Russian caviar bowl and spoon, but the price tag is an eye-watering £600. Elsewhere, Jamie comes across a wacky glass vase that resembles a famous artist’s work, but Philip Serrell thinks it’s no masterpiece. At the sale, both teams hope for big profits, but all they can do is watch as their items go under auctioneer Caroline Hawley’s hammer.

programme.title: Money for Nothing
programme.desc: Jacqui Joseph is patrolling the forecourt of Altrincham recycling centre in Greater Manchester, hoping to find three items that are packed with potential and give them the chance to shine once more. She finds a pair of folding chairs, an old washstand and a collection of glass bottles. Upholsterer Simion Hawtin-Smith and upcycler Sarah Parmenter set to work helping Jacqui transform her finds, but will all three projects produce profits?

programme.title: Escape to the Country
programme.desc: Having spent many happy family holidays in Cornwall, a couple from Hertfordshire now want to make England’s most south-westerly county their permanent home, and Steve Brown is just the man to help them realise their dream. The trio also meet a local ceramicist and take part in a pottery throwdown.

programme.title: The Bidding Room
programme.desc: Nigel Havers presides as members of the public with interesting items to sell come face to face with five dealers who bid against each other to try to bag themselves a bargain. Before facing the dealers, each seller has their item valued by auctioneer Simon Bower. Simon also gives them top tips on the history and key characteristics of their piece, so that when they enter the bidding room, they have all the information they need to try to haggle the best possible price from the dealers. All the dealers are spending their own money but have no idea what the sellers have brought in.

programme.title: Bridge of Lies
programme.desc: Ross Kemp presents the quiz show where a team of four – in this episode, friends Martin, Robyn, Paul and Wayne – take on the Bridge of Lies. One by one, they all face the Bridge, choosing who faces each crossing depending on the question category. Each crossing has 32 potential steps, including 22 truths and ten lies. They must cross the Bridge by stepping on the truths and avoiding the lies, earning money for each correct answer. Step on a lie and the Bridge will halve their money. Step on three lies, and they are out of the game. There is always a safe path across the Bridge. They just have to find it. Once they have each faced the Bridge on their own, those who have been successful will join forces to face the final crossing for a chance to take home the cash.

programme.title: Pointless

programme.title: Panorama
programme.desc: Whether you were wading through floods or struggling through a heatwave, 2026 was the year when you could hardly miss our extreme weather. Temperatures in the summer topped 30C for 33 days in a row. Months earlier, some parts of the UK saw 40 consecutive days of rain. The BBC's climate editor Justin Rowlatt investigates the impact of climate change on our weather. He speaks to scientists who warn that hotter summers and wetter winters are likely to become more typical, and looks at if enough is being done to adapt our towns and cities to the changing climate. Justin asks, as the cost of living continues to bite, are governments under pressure to ditch some green policies, or do they remain committed to tackling climate change?

programme.title: Scotland’s Sacred Islands with Ben Fogle
programme.desc: Ben Fogle explores the ancient sea roads of the Inner Hebrides, with their evocative connections to 6th-century Christian missionaries.
